proposals.evidence: DEDR 1514 directly gives Kodagu tittï, Kolami kis, Malto cicu and Toda tït fire. Badaga kiccə is supported indirectly by the article’s explicit identification of Toda kic as a Badaga loan; this proposal is for the Badaga source form, not for the borrowed Toda song word. Survey titta, kiss, cicadu and tīttə preserve their endings and transcriptions. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 4682 gives Kota maṇḍ and Tulu maṇḍe head, alongside Kannada maṇḍe and the wider maṇṭai skull/head family. Survey Kota manḍə and Tulu manḍa preserve their final vowels. Badaga manḍe and Betta Kurumba maṇḍi are comparative extensions explicitly labelled look-alikes in the source, not literal DEDR attestations. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

Badaga oṭṭe is a comparative extension marked as a look-alike; its missing initial consonant remains visible for review. Malto puḍā preserves its stop transcription. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
